title: Adopt provider-neutral Mac Mini Pi Codex runtime roadmap
businessObjective: Make the Mac Mini, Pi orchestration platform, and replaceable Codex subscription runtime a first-class future deployment option while retaining Tier 0 safety and human authorization.
technicalObjective: Create a derived deployment decision, reconcile permanent roadmap memory, and revise only future backlog packets for provider-neutral intelligence, proposals, worker runtime, executor dispatch, verification, audit, and portability; implement no runtime capability.
architectureReferences: docs/architecture/source/Sri U-Thong Grand Hotel AI OS.md
assumptions: Pi denotes the logical orchestration platform and initially runs as a local service on the same 24/7 Mac Mini host as the supervised worker; Codex owns no durable state.
The first supported provider path is Pi to Codex CLI using ChatGPT subscription authentication; API, local, and other providers remain future disabled alternatives.
The immutable architecture sources remain authoritative and are not edited; this task records a derived deployment decision aligned to them.
acceptanceCriteria: A derived ADR states provider-neutral interfaces, the Mac Mini/Pi/Codex first implementation, Codex non-authorities, Tier 0/shadow bounds, and future provider migration.
Roadmap and future packets define IntelligenceProvider, ProposalGenerator, ExecutorAdapter, and VerificationProvider boundaries; AI cannot authorize its own proposal.

Future packets cover structured intelligence and intervention proposals, Pi-to-Codex adapter, Mac Mini worker/supervision/workspaces/concurrency/timeouts, durable scheduling/queue/DLQ/requeue, subscription health/capacity states, provider-neutral dispatch, audit attribution, independent verification, and fallback qualification.

A distinct future P4-007 packet implements the Codex repository ExecutorAdapter for bounded analysis, code/content changes, tests, branches, pull requests, and repair preparation without policy, approval, scheduling, workflow, or audit authority.

The initial co-located Mac Mini deployment keeps Pi orchestration, durable queue and workflow state, the supervised worker, and the Codex CLI adapter logically separate; durable state survives Pi-service, worker-process, and device restarts and is never Codex ephemeral state.

All exact provider states available, busy, rate_limited, capacity_exhausted, authentication_required, temporarily_unavailable, and disabled fail closed with pause or requeue, evidence, and appropriate notification; no production action occurs.

Only backlog packets and permitted project documents change; completed, active, and P1-006 records, source architecture, runtime code, verifier, schemas, policies, and production surfaces remain untouched.
Affected Phase 2–5 dependency changes are acyclic and documented.

rollbackExpectations: Revert only this task's ADR, project roadmap documents, future backlog packets, task state, and evidence; preserve all completed/current records, immutable sources, and runtime surfaces.
